intuition: Build a valid bracket string one character at a time. An opening bracket starts a pair. A closing bracket must close a pair that is already open. Reject an invalid choice immediately instead of generating every possible string and checking it afterward.

Track two budgets: openings used and closings used. Openings cannot exceed n, and closings cannot overtake openings. These restrictions are enough to describe valid prefixes, so the recursion never needs to repair an invalid one. The path list is shared along the current recursion branch, making append/pop an explicit record of choosing and undoing a character.
Joining occurs only at a complete answer, which separates working storage from the returned strings.

Every recursive prefix has 0 <= closed <= opened <= n. Thus a completed prefix is balanced. Every valid string obeys these inequalities at every prefix, so the recursion follows its characters and eventually emits it. Each character-choice path is unique. Cₙ is the nth Catalan number, the count of valid strings.

The number of valid outputs is the Catalan number C_n. Pair the first opening parenthesis with its matching close: if i pairs lie inside it, n-1-i pairs lie after it. These independent choices give C_n=sum(C_i*C_(n-1-i) for i=0..n-1), with C_0=1. Prefix pruning follows only paths whose closes never exceed opens, so it reaches precisely those C_n leaves.
Each output needs 2n characters, accounting for O(n*C_n) time and output storage.

steps: With n=3, choose opening brackets until path becomes ((( with opened=3 and closed=0.
The opening budget is exhausted; three closings finish ((())).
Backtrack to ((, choose a closing, then open the remaining pair to form (()()).
Further alternate open and close decisions generate (())(), ()(()), and ()()().
Every recorded string has three pairs, and no prefix ever contains more closings than openings.

keyDecision: Add '(' only if opened < n. Add ')' only if closed < opened.

concept.question: How can a bracket string stay valid while we are still building it?
intuition: Generating all strings of opening and closing brackets wastes time on prefixes that are already impossible. A closing bracket cannot be repaired later if it appears before any available opening bracket.

Think of openings as pairs waiting to be closed. We may start a new pair while openings remain in our budget. We may close a pair only when one is currently waiting. Building under these rules keeps every prefix valid.
concept.observation: Never close more pairs than have been opened, and never open more than the requested number of pairs.
approach: Begin with no pairs started or closed.
Explore a legal opening and a legal closing whenever each is available.
Save the string after all requested pairs have been opened and closed.
concept.correctness: The construction rules ensure no prefix has more closings than openings and no result uses more than the pair budget. At completion, the counts agree, so every saved string is valid. Any valid string obeys these same prefix conditions, which means the search can follow all of its choices and will include it.

complexity.space: O(n) auxiliary plus O(n · Cₙ) output
complexity.explanation: Work grows with the number of valid bracket strings, multiplied by the length needed to write each one. The current path and recursion depth are linear in the number of pairs; the output contains all valid strings.

pitfalls: A completed string has twice as many characters as pairs.
A closing cannot appear without a waiting opening.
Undo a choice before exploring another branch.
